newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-MOORE WINS SECOND WEEK IN A ROW.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-MOORE WINS SECOND WEEK IN A ROW.

text.p: Canadian Greg Moore won his second consecutive Indy car race on Sunday at the Detroit Grand Prix when Mauricio Gugelmin and Mark Blundell ran out of fuel on the last lap of the race.

Driving a Reynard Mercedes-Benz Moore, who won last week in Milwaukee, averaged 86.047 mph (138.5 km) to finish 1.818 seconds ahead of Michael Andretti in a Swift Ford and Gil de Ferran of Brazil in a Reynard Honda.

Gugelmin of Brazil and Blundell of Great Britain were running one and two before they ran out of fuel. Gugelmin's tank went dry on the backstraight and Blundell stalled in the last turn within site of the checkered flag and victory on the 2.1 mile (3.3 km) street circuit.
"When I saw Mauricio slow down on the backstraight I thought 'Wow'," said the 22-year-old Moore. "Then I saw Mark stop on the last turn and I thought this was a very early Christmas present."
